## Hands-on 1 – The setup check {#hands-on-1-the-setup-check .smaller}

::: {.small}
**Task 1 – the setup check.** Get to the point where a line of R runs and the data are in front of you.

- **Workspace:** your IDE opens the workspace folder, and `source("R/check_setup.R")` prints an `[OK]` line for every check; the last one fits a number that you will meet again later, `r fmt_num(curve_ref$b, 4)` points of distrust per point of concern
- **Then, while you are online:** `source("R/spec_tools.R"); fetch_multi100()` downloads the file of Task 3 (29 MB) once and checks it
- **Browser lab:** the page has finished loading, the setup cell runs, and `ess` has `r fmt_n(nrow(ess))` rows, one per respondent
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Take the time you need, **into the break** if necessary. Type a green circle in chat when you are through; type **STUCK** and I will come to you.
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
If your installation will not cooperate, do not fight it – open the browser lab and carry on. Every task runs there, and only the reproduction of Task 3 works differently.
:::

::: notes
Your turn, and this first task is deliberately not intellectual. The job is to reach the point where a line of R runs and the data are in front of you. In the workspace, open the folder in your IDE and source the check script: it prints one OK line for each thing that the course needs, and the last check fits a model and prints a number that you will meet again later. Then, while the network is good, run the second line on the slide, which downloads the file that the analysts received and that we need after lunch. In the browser lab, wait for the page, run the setup cell, and check that the data have one row per respondent. Take the time you need, into the break if you have to. A green circle in chat when you are through, STUCK if you need me.
:::
